sections.heading: How to Play Mistweaver
sections.body:
[h2 type=bar toc="How to Play Mistweaver"][color=c10]Mistweaver Monk Rotation in Midnight Season 2[/color][/h2]
Mistweaver Monk's priority and rotation relies entirely on juggling short-duration cooldowns, buffs and procs, and managing mana consumption to be maximized with damage dealt on your group. 

[wrapper width=1100px][box border=true]
[center][table style=grid]
[tr][td]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv12_apextalent_monk_spiritfont size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Align Procs With Damage:[/color][/b] Hold healing procs (like [spell=1260677], [spell=443112]) for heavier incoming damage rather than spending them freely during downtime.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_misc_herb_jadetealeaf size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Keep Mana at the Forefront:[/color][/b] Mana management is a constant priority throughout any encounter. Downtime is your best opportunity to spend [spell=197908] stacks, ensuring you enter the next damage window with the headroom to sustain your output.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[hr]
[table]
	[tr]
	[td width=6%][icon name=inv_12_profession_cooking_tea_green size=medium type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon][/td]
	[td][b][color=c10]Managing Haste:[/color][/b] Haste is one of the more intense aspects of Mistweaver's gameplay. When active, it accelerates your abilities and brings cooldowns back faster, creating high-intensity windows that demand quick decision-making to get the most out of.
	[/td][/tr]
[/table]
[/td][/tr][/table]
[/center]
[/box][/wrapper]

sections.heading: Responding to Incoming Damage
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Responding to Incoming Damage" type=bar][color=monk][icon name=ability_monk_uplift type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Mistweaver Monk Responding to Incoming Damage[/color][/h2]
[tabs name="responding" uniform=true iconborders=true]
	[tab name="Single Target" icon=ability_monk_vivify]
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Single Target[/color][/h3]
		Single target healing is one of Mistweaver's core strengths. Our toolkit allows for quick, flexible responses to incoming damage, with options that scale based on how much time you have to react. In this context, "single target" refers to healing one individual - whether that's a tank, a party member, or yourself.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=covenant-necrolord]Light Single Target Damage[/color][/h3]
			Light damage consists of small, non-threatening hits that don't demand immediate attention which is handled naturally by your HoTs - primarily [spell=115151] that scales with your lowest-hp ally via [spell=1280297]. Since you should already be maintaining HoTs on the group, minimal additional action is needed when someone takes light damage.

			With [spell=467293] talented, leveraging the damage-to-heal conversion to continue attacking while healing the injured ally is a smart move. [spell=388023] intelligently splits its total healing evenly between (up to 5) injured allies, meaning a single injured player receives the full heal. This allows you to maintain damage output in a mana-efficient way without wasting procs that could be saved for heavier damage phases.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4]Medium Single Target Damage[/color][/h3]
			Medium damage typically involves a single hit that drops an ally to roughly 50% health. Your response depends on whether additional damage is incoming.

			If follow-up damage is expected, [spell=116849] is your safest option, but might be more beneficial for [color=c6]heavy damage[/color]. The absorb buys you breathing room for continuous healing on your target. Use this at your own discretion.

			If no follow-up damage is expected, assess your available procs. A [spell=443110] proc, for instance, can quickly apply a powerful [spell=124682] HoT while providing group-wide shields effectively handling the situation without further input. Similarly, [spell=1260565] is an even stronger version of the previous, as its healing is redirected from split-between-five to fully on the single injured target alongside applying [spell=406139]s on your group, though this could be instead saved for AoE damage.

			For both Raid and Mythic+ content, [spell=116670]/[spell=399491] serve as your primary quick-response tools. When paired with [spell=388812], these become instant-cast, enabling rapid reactions to further damage on the target. However, they come with trade-offs: high mana costs, consumption of procs better suited for AoE healing, and in Sheilun's Gift's case, the use of stacked clouds that could deliver stronger AoE healing.

			As with [color=covenant-necrolord]light damage[/color], Jadefire Teachings talented allows you to maintain pressing [spell=107428] on cooldown in order to keep consistent maintenance healing rolling.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c6]Heavy Single Target Damage[/color][/h3]
			Heavy damage scenarios include sustained high-damage DoTs, tanks taking sustained damage without defensive cooldowns, or party members who've pulled aggro. Since we already discussed using [spell=116849] in [color=c4]medium damage[/color] situations, [color=c6]heavy damage[/color] is the natural point to fully commit to the external.

			This is where you'll reach for Mistweaver's strongest single-target healing tool: [spell=115175]. Beyond making your Vivify, Sheilun's Gift, and Enveloping Mist instant cast during the channel, it also provides passive healing through its own HoT effect and additional damage reduction from [spell=388681] at the cost of one extra (though shortened) global cooldown. It's worth noting that this sequence is only necessary when you need to cast several Vivify or Sheilun's Gifts back-to-back on a single target in genuine danger, not as a default response. If the previous damage tiers ([color=covenant-necrolord]light[/color] and [color=c4]medium[/color]) are still holding things together, there's no need to escalate here.
			[rotation-timeline]
				[rt-step=115175]
				[rt-step=124682 text="Optional but preferred"]
				[rt-step=116670 start end loop-text="Until stable"]
			[/rotation-timeline]
		
	[/tab]

	[tab name="AoE" icon=inv12_apextalent_monk_spiritfont]
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]AoE[/color][/h3]
		AoE healing is where Mistweaver truly shines. With the right setup, you can keep your entire party alive through heavy damage phases. The key is being proactive rather than reactive, entering damage events already ramped and ready to perform, though there will be moments where you need quick reactions to incoming damage.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=covenant-necrolord]Light AoE Damage[/color][/h3]
			Light AoE damage consists of small hits across multiple allies that don't require immediate attention. This is where your HoTs, especially [spell=115151], do most of the heavy lifting. Keeping them up on your group allows for passive healing that handles light AoE without needing to actively spend globals.

			With [spell=467293] talented, you can continue dealing damage while healing multiple injured allies with [spell=388023]. It splits its total healing evenly among up to 5 injured targets, making it an efficient way to handle light AoE without burning procs better saved for heavier phases.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c4]Medium AoE Damage[/color][/h3]
			This is where you need to actively respond to incoming damage. As a general rule, begin thinking about cooldown usage here. Mistweaver has several at its disposal: [spell=115310], [spell=322118]/[spell=325197], [spell=443028], and [spell=116680] (the latter functioning as a minor cooldown given its attached effects). Ideally, you've already ramped ahead of the damage, so your HoTs and amplifying effects are in place to maximize their value. See the [url=www.wowhead.com/guide/33321#responding-ramping]ramping[/url] and [url=www.wowhead.com/guide/33321#major-cooldowns]major cooldowns[/url] sections for more detail.

			Procs in medium damage are no longer held; they're spent to handle outgoing damage, so use them wisely:
			[ul]
			[li][spell=443110] procs should be directed at targets actively taking damage to maximize [spell=124682]'s HoT and the group-wide shields.[/li]
			[li][spell=1260565] procs are equally valuable here, providing strong split healing that naturally favors injured targets over time, along with [spell=406139]s on your group.
			[ul]
			[li]The second and third points of Spiritfont amplify abilities you're already casting: [spell=107428] (particularly with Jadefire Teachings for consistent maintenance healing) and Enveloping Mist's HoT, respectively.[/li]
			[/ul][/li]
			[/ul]

			A few [spell=116670]/[spell=399491] casts can quickly spot-heal those in the most danger, especially when paired with [spell=388812] for instant casts. Just be mindful of the mana cost, and consider whether those procs are better saved for a heavier damage phase ahead. Keep in mind, taking a big [spell=115869] chug to gain stacks via [spell=1270621] grants Sheilun's Gift a stronger AoE heal as opposed to mostly being single-target focused.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c6]Heavy AoE Damage[/color][/h3]
			Heavy damage is where cooldowns stop being optional and become a requirement. Everything from the [color=c4]medium damage[/color] phase still applies, but cooldown usage is now guaranteed, and back-to-back cooldowns are sometimes necessary to keep up with the incoming damage.

			This section isn't quite too long, but the key point is that for heavy damage, it is almost always sustained long enough that you are holding onto the points made in medium damage for prolonged periods of time, often utilizing cooldowns back-to-back to keep up with the damage. For instance, you might find yourself pressing [spell=115310] during a large dip of damage while [spell=325197] is active, and then following up the cooldown with large stacked [spell=399491] at the end to top off the damage.

			During heavy damage, make sure to strategically and continuously hop between players using [spell=116670]/[spell=399491] to ensure you're healing the most injured targets, not allowing them to die. [spell=116849] is a phenomenal external that we can make use of in these moments, as we can practically ignore a player during the heavy damage. 
	[/tab]

	[tab name="Ramping" icon=spell_monk_envelopingmist]
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Ramping[/color][/h3]
			Almost all healers have some form of a ramp: a way to build up healing ahead of incoming damage. Mistweaver is no exception, using short-duration HoTs to create powerful burst windows that can be timed directly around incoming damage spikes.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Mythic+[/color][/h3]
			In Mythic+, the number of [spell=124682] casts required within a ramp scales directly with the incoming damage. As key levels increase, more casts are needed, and the time spent ramping grows accordingly.

			Ramping is not a strict requirement to perform well, but it is a powerful tool that pays off significantly when mastered. The general process is as follows:

			[rotation-timeline]
				[rt-step=115151 text="Dump all charges"]
				[rt-step=115175]
				[rt-step=124682 text="3-4x"]
				[rt-step=107428 text="To extend"]
			[/rotation-timeline]

			For lighter incoming damage, fewer Enveloping Mist casts are sufficient, and prioritizing your squishiest party members is generally the right call.

			Soothing Mist in general is covered further in the [url=www.wowhead.com/guide/33321#advanced-soothing-mist]Advanced Soothing Mist[/url] section, but it is worth noting here that the time savings from [spell=115175] only kick in after the second Enveloping Mist cast. Avoid using it as a ramp tool unless you're committing to 3 or more casts in a row.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Raid[/color][/h3]
			Ramping in Raid is less flexible than Mythic+, as our gameplay is largely built around cooldown windows with maintenance healing in between. Ramps revolve around strategic [spell=443294] windows, which return faster cooldown rates and allow us to place and immediately extend several [spell=115151]s across the group, followed by cooldowns to cleave healing onto the raid.

			A second form of ramping involves using [spell=322118] earlier than damage hits to line up [spell=116670] with high incoming damage. See the [url=www.wowhead.com/guide/33321#major-cooldowns]major cooldowns[/url] section for more detail on the Yu'lon ramp specifically.
	[/tab]
[/tabs]

sections.heading: Major Cooldowns
sections.body:
[h2 toc="Major Cooldowns" type=bar][color=monk][icon name=spell_monk_revival type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Mistweaver Monk Major Cooldowns[/color][/h2]

Mistweaver Monks have a wide variety of cooldowns available to use that offer differing profiles of healing requirements, though some can and do get molded to match whatever might be necessary to counter! Knowing how you can utilize these cooldowns over others allows for quicker understanding and mastering of the specialization without question.

[pad]

[tabs name="cds" uniform=true iconborders=true]
[tab name="Thunder Focus Tea" icon=ability_monk_thunderfocustea]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Thunder Focus Tea[/color][/h3]
[spell=116680]'s synergy with Mistweaver's kit is [i]extensive[/i] and is thought to be one of Mistweaver's most overloaded buttons due to these interactions. Though not specifically seen in the same caliber of a cooldown as something plannable like [spell=115310], it can be considered a "rotational" cooldown and one that can (& should!) be paired with other cooldowns to give more... oomph!

At a baseline, the spell is incredibly simple in its functions: it empowers the next spell cast to grant that spell additional functionality:
[ul]
[li][spell=124682] - Instantly place an Enveloping Mist on your target, ignoring the original cast time, while also healing them instantly for the total HoT amount.[/li]
[li][spell=115151] - Increase the duration of the resulting Renewing Mist by +10 seconds.[/li]
[li][spell=185099] - Reduce the incoming cooldown of Rising Sun Kick by 9 seconds.[/li]
[/ul]

However, there are several talents that we can choose from that strengthen Thunder Focus Tea further: 
[ul]
[li][spell=1260680] - Guarantees a [spell=1260565] stack as soon as you press Thunder Focus Tea.[/li]
[li][spell=197895] - Grants an additional usage of an empower per Thunder Focus Tea cast.[/li]
[li][spell=388491] - Grants a semi-permanent buff that increases a Secondary Stat relative to the chosen empowered ability.
[ul]
[li]Enveloping Mist - Grants [spell=388498] (Critical Strike).[/li]
[li]Renewing Mist - Grants [spell=388497] (Haste).[/li]
[li]Rising Sun Kick - Grants [spell=388500] (Versatility).[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[li][spell=1277302] - Instantly resets the remaining cooldown on Rising Sun Kick.[/li]
[li][spell=1242910] - Places a [npc=60849] at your feet.[/li]
[/ul]

Along those lines, there are many "combos" we can choose to do with Thunder Focus Tea to make gameplay a bit more interesting with weaving in different abilities that might not be the most clear at first glance. Take a look at the [url=www.wowhead.com/guide/33321#advanced-thunder-focus-tea]Advanced Thunder Focus Tea[/url] section for more details.

[hr]
Though both Hero Trees add additional benefits to [spell=116680], there are distinct differences in their use cases.

Specifically with [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color], our aim is to use [spell=116680] as often as possible, given that its own cast offers quickened cooldown rates to itself (and other spells!) via [spell=443294]. Sitting on the cooldown is effectively a [b]healing loss[/b] the longer it sits off cooldown, especially if [spell=443294] is active when it should be actively cooling down during this window. 

On the other hand, [symbol=wow-hero-talent-master-of-harmony] [color=#6ED4CD]Master of Harmony[/color]'s [spell=450892]'s two charges give us flexibility on its usage, meaning that holding onto one charge of the cooldown to pair with damage events and/or other cooldowns (without overcapping both charges) is integral to the success of the cooldown. The surrounding after-effects of applying [spell=450769] HoTs on your group during the [color=#6ED4CD]vitality[/color] withdraw window of [spell=450508] simply add to its strengths.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]
Strong rotationally, stronger paired with CDs.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color]: Use it or lose it.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][symbol=wow-hero-talent-master-of-harmony] [color=#6ED4CD]Master of Harmony[/color]: Press wisely.[/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Invoke Yu'lon" icon=ability_monk_dragonkick]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Invoke Yu'lon, the Jade Serpent[/color][/h3]

One of the two August Celestials of Pandaria we can call to our aid in combat, [spell=322118], provides passive healing on her own while reducing the mana cost of [spell=124682] significantly during her active window. This cooldown demands constant activity to maximize its value - Yu'lon rewards players who actively cast throughout her duration.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]The Yu'lon Gameplay[/h3]

During her window, you should cast multiple [spell=124682][color=q]s[/color] in sequence on different players to:

[ul]
[li]Generate multiple [spell=115151] buffs via [spell=388847][/li]
[li]Set up massive [spell=274586] healing by following with [spell=116670] casts[/li]
[li]Heal those affected by [spell=124682]![/li]
[/ul]

With [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color], when you first invoke her, your first [spell=100780] or [spell=116670] cast will trigger [spell=443087], which in turn activates [spell=443110].

Every [spell=124682] you cast generates a [spell=115151] that reduces [spell=107428]'s cooldown through [spell=173841]. While this accelerated pace can feel overwhelming at first, stick to your spell priority and cast abilities as you normally would\u2014the speed will become natural with practice.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Talent Modifiers[/h3]

Several talents directly enhance Yu'lon's power:

[ul]
[li][spell=343655] applies [spell=406139] to 5 allies instantly when Yu'lon is invoked, granting small absorb shields. Additionally, this talent increases your [spell=124682] cast speed by 30% while Yu'lon is active.[/li]
[li]You must choose between two playstyle-defining talents:
[ul]
[li][spell=388212] - Reduces the cooldown from 2 minutes to 1 minute, but halves the duration. This creates more frequent burst windows with shorter uptime.[/li]
[li][spell=388031] - Maintains the 2-minute cooldown while significantly amplifying Yu'lon's power:
[ul]
[li]When [spell=343655]'s Chi Cocoons break, they apply a fresh 4-second [spell=124682] to each target[/li]
[li]Yu'lon's passive [spell=343737] healing is increased by 500%[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[/ul]
[/li]
[/ul]

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Yu'lon Cast Sequence Timeline[/h3]

[rotation-timeline]
[rt-step-group=115151 text="Use all charges"]
[rt-sup=116680]
[/rt-step-group]
[rt-step=107428]
[rt-step=322118]
[rt-step=115175 start loop-text="Cast Enveloping Mists until Rising Sun Kick is off cooldown, capitalize damage events with Vivify until the cooldown is over" text="If mana allows"]
[rt-step=124682 text="Cast until RSK is off CD"]
[rt-step=124682]
[rt-step=124682]
[rt-step=107428]
[rt-step=116670 text="Damage event occurs" end]
[/rotation-timeline]

[b]Important:[/b] You can now switch targets freely during your [spell=115175] channel, and the channeled beam will automatically follow your new target. For maximum efficiency, cast [spell=115175] before using several consecutive [spell=124682] and [spell=116670] to take advantage of the reduced global cooldown. When doing this, ensure you're casting [spell=124682] on different targets that are currently taking damage or will be taking damage soon, similar to casting [spell=116670] on the most-injured targets within your group.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]
High-activity cooldown that rewards constant casting with massive throughput.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Spam [spell=124682] during the window to set up [spell=274586] healing.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Gift of the Celestials: Aggressive, frequent casts. Jade Bond: Extended, paced gameplay.[/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Invoke Chi-Ji" icon=inv_pet_cranegod]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Invoke Chi-Ji, the Red Crane[/color][/h3]

One of the two August Celestials of Pandaria we can call to our aid in combat, [spell=325197], delivers most of his healing through [spell=343819] casts. These healing events trigger whenever you use [spell=100784], [spell=107428], or [spell=101546], converting your damage into group healing.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]The Chi-Ji Gameplay[/h3]

During his window, Chi-Ji provides healing through two distinct mechanics:
[ul]
[li]Granting instant-cast [spell=124682] with reduced mana cost[/li]
[li]Healing your allies with [spell=343819] as you press melee abilities[/li]
[/ul]

This dual approach creates an incredibly active gameplay loop. Your melee abilities become far more powerful than their standard [spell=388023] damage-to-healing conversions, while simultaneously allowing you to spot-heal injured targets with instant Enveloping Mist casts. These heal-over-time effects not only deliver strong immediate value but also amplify all subsequent healing dealt to those targets through the heal-amp effect.

While Chi-Ji is active and you're talented into the [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color] Hero Talent Tree, your first [spell=100780] or [spell=116670] cast will trigger [spell=443087], which activates [spell=443110]. Consume this buff immediately for a substantial healing boost.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Understanding Gust of Mists[/h3]

Chi-Ji's [spell=343819] healing may seem straightforward, but understanding the mechanics allows you to maximize your output. Each melee ability triggers Chi-Ji to heal two different targets with three instances of Gust of Mists, generating six total healing events per trigger.

[spell=107428] and [spell=101546] always generate exactly six healing instances, regardless of any modifiers. However, [spell=100784] scales with your [spell=116645] stacks: each additional Blackout Kick from Teachings of the Monastery adds six more healing events, up to a maximum of 30 gusts at 4 stacks.

The scaling breakdown:

Vice versa, the more rot-based the damage is, the fewer stacks are required to gain consistent healing throughput.

Several talents directly enhance Chi-Ji's power:
[ul]
[li][spell=343655] applies [spell=406220] to 5 allies instantly when Chi-Ji is invoked, granting small absorb shields. Additionally, Chi-Ji grants you four [spell=116645] stacks immediately upon invocation, eliminating your ramp-up requirement and letting you dive straight into high-output healing.[/li]
[li]You must choose between two playstyle-defining talents:
[ul]
[li][spell=388212] - Reduces the cooldown from 2 minutes to 1 minute, but halves the duration. This creates more frequent damage-to-healing windows with aggressive, burst-focused gameplay.[/li]
[li][spell=388031] - Maintains the 2-minute cooldown while significantly amplifying Chi-Ji's power:
[ul]
[li]When [spell=343655]'s Chi Cocoons break, they apply a fresh 4-second [spell=124682] to each target[/li]

[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]

Damage-focused cooldown that converts combat actions into massive passive healing.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Press melee abilities -> do additional healing.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Weave instant [spell=124682] casts on injured targets to amplify follow-up healing.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Gift of the Celestials: Aggressive, frequent windows. Jade Bond: Extended, empowered gameplay.[/li]
[/ul]

[tab name="Revival / Restoral" icon=spell_monk_revival]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Revival[/color][/h3]
An iconic spell in Mistweaver's spellbook - [spell=115310]. This long-cooldown ability delivers all of its healing upfront in a single global cooldown, hitting every single member of your group the moment you activate it. This makes Revival one of the most powerful panic heals in the game, capable of instantly stabilizing your entire raid during critical moments.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Healing and Dispelling[/h3]
Beyond its raw healing power, Revival carries an additional benefit: it dispels Poison, Disease, and Magic-based effects from every ally it touches. Due to PvP balancing, Revival can only remove up to 3 effects from a single target, but it will dispel every single ally that the spell reaches. This makes it exceptionally powerful for encounters that apply multiple painful debuffs requiring immediate removal across the entire raid.

Functionally, Mistweavers will tend to want to pair the cooldown with a moment of dispelling, but it is important to note that Revival functionally heals [b]first[/b] [i]then[/i] dispels, not allowing for those pesky bomb-like dispels that deal damage across the entire raid to be dispelled then healed.

[h3 type=bar toc=false][icon name=ability_monk_tigerstyle size=small type=round color=c10 inline=true][/icon] Restoral - The Safer Alternative[/h3]
We have the option of talenting into Revival's counterpart, [spell=388615], which trades away the ability to dispel Magic-based effects in exchange for more controlled usage. This choice is typically made in Raid encounters where mass-dispelling magical effects could trigger catastrophic consequences.

For example, during the [npc=223779] encounter on Mythic difficulty, dispelling [spell=438677] from the entire raid simultaneously can cause a raid wipe. In these scenarios, Restoral allows healers to handle dispels individually while preserving the emergency healing component of the cooldown for any critical moment. An added bonus: Restoral can be cast while stunned, though this has limited PvE applications.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Talent Modifiers[/h3]
Mistweaver has a single talent that enhances Revival: [spell=388551]. This talent reduces the cooldown from 3 minutes to 2 minutes 30 seconds while also increasing Revival's healing output by 15%. The shorter cooldown allows for more frequent emergency uses throughout an encounter, making it valuable in fights with multiple dangerous damage spikes.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]
Instant raid-wide heal with mass dispel utility.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Revival: Full power with Magic dispels - watch for dangerous debuffs.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Restoral: Safer healing-only option when mass dispels are risky.[/li]
[/ul]
[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Life Cocoon" icon=ability_monk_chicocoon]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Life Cocoon[/color][/h3]
Mistweaver's external comes in the form of [spell=116849], which visually wraps an ally in a bright green bubble and lifts them off the ground, ensuring their safety for a limited duration. This ability applies a large absorb shield to its target, protecting them from all forms of damage while they're encased in the cocoon.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Strength of the External[/h3]

While it's not damage reduction in the traditional sense, Life Cocoon is an incredibly powerful external tool for both DPS and healers. It excels in both proactive and reactive situations, but understanding how absorbs work compared to damage reduction is key to maximizing its value.

Consider this example: A player is sitting at 10,000 health (10% of their max health). If they receive a damage reduction external like [spell=33206], their effective health pool increases by 40% to 14,000 damage before death. Now let's say we, the Mistweaver about to cast [spell=116849], have 100,000 health. Our Life Cocoon would provide an absorb shield worth 48,000 points of damage, bringing that player's effective health pool to 58,000 points of damage before death.

[b]The lower your target's health, the more valuable Life Cocoon becomes at preventing their death.[/b] That said, even on healthy targets, a 48,000-point absorb shield remains incredibly valuable when players lack their own damage reduction cooldowns or when heavy incoming damage is expected.

Life Cocoon also shines in soak mechanics\u2014Mistweavers can often use their external to solo soak mechanics that would normally require multiple players or defensive cooldowns.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Talent Modifiers[/h3]
Your talent tree offers several powerful modifiers to enhance Life Cocoon:
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=388548] creates a reactive lifesaving tool by applying both [spell=115151] and [spell=124682] to low-health targets, provided the absorb shield holds[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=388218] increases the absorb shield by a whopping 80%, dramatically boosting its potency[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=202424] reduces the cooldown to 75 seconds while shortening the duration, allowing for more frequent life-saving uses throughout an encounter[/li]
[/ul]

[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]
Massive absorb that scales better the lower your target's health.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Save lives reactively or enable risky plays proactively.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Don't be afraid to use it - dead DPS do no damage.[/li]
[/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Sheilun's Gift" icon=inv12_ability_monk_sheilunsgift]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Sheilun's Gift[/color][/h3]
A once iconic artifact trait from the mighty [item=128937], wielded by [npc=73303], lends us his power in the form of [spell=399491] - an AoE group-heal that generates clouds around the Mistweaver during combat. Each cloud amplifies the healing power of your next cast, stacking up to create massive burst healing potential.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]How It Works[/h3]
In this iteration, Sheilun's Gift functions as a replacement for [spell=116670], inheriting nearly all of Vivify's modifying talents while adding its own unique benefits. Clouds generate passively every 8 seconds while in combat and persist until you leave combat for 60 seconds, allowing you to build and maintain stacks between pulls.

Any talent that mentions Vivify will also apply to Sheilun's Gift, with one critical exception: [spell=274586]. With Invigorating Mists, Vivify, and Sheilun's Gift operate as separate spells. Vivify triggers the standard effect (healing all allies with [spell=115151]), while Sheilun's Gift receives a massive 500% healing increase on its primary target only. This makes target selection crucial - always cast Sheilun's Gift on your most injured ally to maximize the benefit of this interaction.

Even at 0 stacks, Sheilun's Gift functions as a stronger version of Vivify by cleaving healing onto multiple targets. As clouds accumulate, the spell transforms into one of the most powerful spot-heal tools in your arsenal.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Timing and Usage[/h3]
Understanding when to spam Sheilun's Gift versus holding it for incoming damage is key to mastering the ability. You can strategically time your cast to land right as AoE damage hits your group, delivering a massive emergency heal. Balance cloud generation with tactical usage - sometimes saving stacks for a critical moment is more valuable than spending them immediately.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Talent Modifiers[/h3]
Core Modifiers (Nearly Mandatory):
[ul]
[li][spell=400053] - Doubles cloud generation speed from every 8 seconds to every 4 seconds, dramatically accelerating your ramp-up.[/li]
[li][spell=1270621] - Transforms [spell=115869] into a cloud-generation tool, granting 1 cloud per stack of Mana Tea consumed.[/li]
[/ul]
Playstyle Modifiers (Situational):
[ul]
[li][spell=404408] - Converts Sheilun's Gift from a 3-target heal (1 primary + 2 random allies) to a guaranteed 5-target heal, while reducing the cast time by 0.5 seconds. Exceptional for 5-man content, where you'll hit the entire group every cast.[/li]
[li][spell=471761] - Shifts from AoE to single-target focus, increasing healing on the primary target by 20% and making every cast instant. Perfect for spot-healing priority targets.[/li]
[/ul]
[h3 type=bar toc=false]TLDR[/h3]
Vivify replacement that builds stacks for massive burst healing.
[ul]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Always target the lowest health ally for maximum [spell=274586] value.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right]Time high-stack casts with incoming damage for clutch saves.[/li]
[li icon=angle-double-right][spell=404408] for dungeons, [spell=471761] for single-target priority.[/li]
[/ul]

[pad]
[/tab]

[tab name="Celestial Conduit" icon=inv_ability_conduitofthecelestialsmonk_celestialconduit]
[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=monk]Celestial Conduit[/color][/h3]

[spell=443028], given to us if we decide to be a [symbol=wow-hero-talent-conduit-of-the-celestials] [color=#67ECAF]Conduit of the Celestials[/color], delivers substantial healing to allies and damage to enemies over a short channeled duration, and should be used as frequently as your group requires. This is the gateway to [spell=443589], the capstone talent Hero Tree, which summons all four August Celestials alongside empowered versions of their associated talents. The cooldown's power is split roughly 50/50 between the channeled healing and the celestial summon effects.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Summoning the Celestials[/h3]
While channeling Celestial Conduit, you can press the ability again to summon the August Celestials early\u2014though they'll also arrive automatically when the channel completes (or, if interrupted, where the channel [i]would have[/i] completed). This flexibility allows you to decide when their effects trigger:
[ul]
[li][spell=443087] and [spell=443255] deliver immediate burst healing
[ul][li]Note that Flight of the Red Crane no longer exists as a standalone effect and only occurs with Unity Within.[/li][/ul]
[/li]
[li][spell=443110] applies absorb shields to multiple allies[/li]
[li][spell=443294] accelerates the cooldown of affected spells[/li]
[/ul]
The key decision point: if you've positioned yourself to avoid losing casts due to Yu'lon's cooldown acceleration, you can summon the Celestials early to access their effects sooner. Otherwise, let the channel complete naturally to maximize the value of each cast.

[h3 type=bar toc=false]Managing Yu'lon's "Haste"[/h3]
While most Celestial effects are automatic, [spell=443294] requires active management. For 8 seconds, Yu'lon reduces the cooldown time of [spell=115151], [spell=107428], [spell=116680], and [spell=116849] by 150%\u2014effectively making them come off cooldown 2.5x faster.

With [spell=173841] talented, the rapid-fire cooldown reduction on Renewing Mist and Rising Sun Kick can feel overwhelming at first. The rotation speeds up dramatically, with abilities becoming available much faster than you're accustomed to. Success will come from acclimating to the accelerated pace and reacting quickly to those abilities as they come off cooldown.

[h2 toc="Advanced Tips" type=bar][color=c10][icon name=inv_staff_2h_artifactmonkeyking_d_05 type=round size=medium inline=true color=c10][/icon] Mistweaver Monk Advanced Tips[/color][/h2]

[tabs name="advanced" uniform=true iconborders=true]
	[tab name="Renewing Mist" icon=ability_monk_renewingmists]
                [h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Renewing Mist Jumps[/color][/h3]
[spell=115151] is an interesting ability that we use constantly in all forms of content, but it has some unique pieces of functionality worth highlighting to ensure you're getting the most out of it. The multiple-charged spell has a clever component: if the HoT effect heals a target past their maximum health (overhealing), it will attempt to jump to another random eligible target. An eligible target is one that is:
[ul]
[li]Within 20 yards of the player who has the Renewing Mist[/li]
[li]Does not already have a Renewing Mist[/li]
[li]Is injured[/li]
[/ul]
A jump will also be triggered if you cast a fresh Renewing Mist on a target that already has one, as the older Renewing Mist gets replaced and jumps away but again, [i]only[/i] if there is an eligible target. This portion of the spell's functionality makes it incredibly good for spreading healing across your group, as it will (almost) always be on a target that is injured, causing little overhealing unless there are no eligible targets for it to jump to.

"Can I press Renewing Mist on myself and have it auto-target?" is a question that comes up often, but the answer is "not necessarily." If you cast Renewing Mist on yourself (or another target consistently) and then cast another one, the old one will attempt to jump to another target. If an eligible target exists, it will jump to them. If there is no eligible target (meaning no injured allies within 20 yards who don't already have a Renewing Mist), the old one will simply pandemic on yourself, adding duration up to +30% of its original value. In that case, you've [b]effectively lost a Renewing Mist for your group[/b] since no eligible targets were in range, even if there were injured allies just outside that 20-yard window.

Thanks to [spell=388701], we can use this mechanic to our advantage by intentionally targeting someone who already has Renewing Mist to force a jump, giving it a chance to immediately split via the talent. That said, it's a [b]high-risk, high-reward[/b] play since if there are no eligible targets within 20 yards, the Renewing Mist will simply refresh on the same target rather than splitting, making a [i]big[/i] loss for your overall healing.

Dancing Mists, though, naturally does this during high intensity healing where health bars are jumping to 100% and back down rapidly, as Renewing Mists are flying between targets at an incredible pace.
	[/tab]
	
	[tab name="Soothing Mist" icon=ability_monk_soothingmists]
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Soothing Mist[/color][/h3]
			[spell=115175] is a channeled, 8-second long healing over time spell that grants you the ability to instantly cast [spell=116670], [spell=399491], and [spell=124682] during its channeled duration. Unique to Soothing Mist, the mana cost of the spell is built into the channel its self, meaning that you are paying the mana-tax for every tick of the spell rather than entirely upfront. Let's break Soothing Mist down into several of its key components.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Global Cooldown[/color][/h3]
			The global cooldown is a 1.5-second cooldown (lowered by haste) that is triggered after every spell cast across the entire game. Soothing Mist has a special exception to this rule: its activation only triggers a 1-second global cooldown. This is important to keep in mind as we discuss the later sections, since this can potentially save us time (or cost us time) when we utilize the instant casts granted by Soothing Mist.
	
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Instant Casts[/color][/h3]
			A major boon to Soothing Mist is the ability to instantly cast [spell=116670], [spell=399491], and [spell=124682] during its channel. Each ability triggers the 1.5-second global cooldown as normal, but happen at the beginning of the global cooldown (immediately) rather than at the end of their respective casts (if used without Soothing Mist).

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Enveloping Mist[/color][/h3]

			In Enveloping Mist's case, we take the 2-second base cast time and reduce it to an instant, invoking the 1.5-second global cooldown instead. This saves 0.5 seconds per cast, however we have to account for the 1-second global cooldown from Soothing Mist's activation. If casting only a single Enveloping Mist, the time savings are completely negated by the Soothing Mist global cooldown, resulting in a 0.5-second time [i]loss[/i] rather than a [i]gain[/i].

			You could argue that the faster application of Enveloping Mist combined with the extra HoT ticking from Soothing Mist is worth the time loss, but the counterpoint is that we could have been pressing other abilities more quickly that might do more healing overall.

			As shown below, the time savings from Soothing Mist only kick in after the second Enveloping Mist cast. Avoid using Soothing Mist before Enveloping Mist casts unless you are certain you will be casting several abilities afterward for emergency healing or ramping multiple Enveloping Mists.
			[pad]
			[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/32408.png]
		
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Vivify and Sheilun's Gift[/color][/h3]

			For Vivify (and by extension Sheilun's Gift with [spell=404408] talented, which we would have at all times), the base cast time is already 1.5 seconds, the same as the global cooldown. This means there is no time saving when casting either of these spells inside Soothing Mist, though you do receive the healing slightly faster as a result. You should never use Soothing Mist before a single cast of Vivify or Sheilun's Gift, as there is no time saving to be had.

			As shown in the graph, we will consistently be 1 second behind if we choose to open with Soothing Mist before several casts.
			[pad]
			[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/32472.png]

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Both[/color][/h3]

			Considering that healing is returned faster for both spell casts, when you need emergency healing on a target that requires several casts back to back, Soothing Mist is your best option, albeit at a slight 0.5-second time loss overall since we gained 0.5 seconds on the instant Enveloping Mist cast.

			[img src=https://wow.zamimg.com/uploads/guide/images/32473.png]

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Jade Serpent Statue[/color][/h3]
			[spell=115313] is a Class Tree talent that can be used in conjunction with Soothing Mist for additional healing via the statue's passive. When the statue is active and you begin channeling Soothing Mist, the statue will begin channeling its own Soothing Mist on the same target, effectively increasing the total Soothing Mist healing by 1.5x for the duration. Even if your channel ends early, the statue will continue its own Soothing Mist channel for the full 8-second duration.

	[/tab]


	[tab name="Teachings of the Monastery" icon=passive_monk_teachingsofmonastery]
		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Teachings of the Monastery[/color][/h3]
		Mistweaver has a baseline mechanic that drives a few of our spec's interactions in [spell=202090]. This passive grants us a stack of the self-named buff for every [spell=100780] that strikes an enemy, up to a maximum of 4 stacks. With each stack, an additional [spell=100784] hits the enemy with each having an individual chance of 20% to reset the remaining cooldown on [spell=107428]. This gives us some room to play with probability and chance to aim for resets on one of our core abilities throughout the kit.

		With [spell=388779], aim for 2 stacks before pressing Blackout Kick. With [spell=1243155], press Blackout Kick at 0 stacks. The math behind these different strategies reveals why GCD efficiency matters more than raw reset chance.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Rising Sun Kick Reset Probability[/color][/h3]
		More Blackout Kick hits means better odds at a reset. Each hit independently rolls a 20% chance to reset Rising Sun Kick, so the probability of getting [i]at least one[/i] reset scales with your Teachings of the Monastery stacks:
		[code]Reset chance = 1 - (0.8) ^ (1 + stacks)[/code]

		[tr]
		[td align=center][b][color=gem10][spell=202090] Stacks[/color][/b][/td]
		[td align=center][b][color=gem10][spell=100784] Hits[/color][/b][/td]

		While more stacks always mean a higher absolute reset chance, the real question isn't "how likely is a reset?" but rather "how many GCDs did I spend building those stacks?" This is where [spell=388779] and [spell=1243155] diverge sharply in their approach to resets.

		[h3 type=bar toc=false][color=c10]Way of the Crane[/color][/h3]
		With [spell=388779], each Tiger Palm strikes the enemy twice, granting 2 Teachings of the Monastery stacks per cast. This means you reach meaningful stack counts in fewer GCDs, changing the optimal strategy for resets entirely.
